# Quadra: QUality Assessment of Dimensionality Reduction Algorithms

Quadra is an R package for measuring how well a dimensionality-reduction
embedding preserves structure from the input data.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub with
[pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/):

``` r

pak::pak("jlmelville/quadra")
```

Quadra requires rnndescent 0.3.0 or later. If you are upgrading a source
installation, rebuild Quadra after updating rnndescent so its compiled
code uses the new distance functions.

Quadra contains C++ code, so installing from source requires the
appropriate build tools. On Windows, install
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/). On macOS, see
the [R for macOS
FAQ](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/RMacOSX-FAQ.html#Installation-of-source-packages)
if compilation or linking fails.

## Quick Start

Nearest-neighbor preservation asks how many of each observation’s
input-space neighbors remain neighbors in the embedding. Here is a small
PCA example:

``` r

library(quadra)

iris_x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
iris_pca <- stats::prcomp(iris_x, rank. = 2)$x

nn_preservation(
  iris_x, iris_pca, k = c(5, 15),
  nn_method_in = "brute"
)
```

Here `nnp5` is 0.64. On average, the PCA plot keeps just over three of
each flower’s five nearest neighbors. Five neighbors chosen at random
from the other 149 flowers would give an expected score of about 0.034.
Widen the neighborhood to 15 flowers and the fraction retained rises to
about 0.80.

## Learn More

The [metric
overview](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/metrics-overview.html)
helps you choose a measure and decide whether to score the whole dataset
or a sample. For individual metrics, see the guides to [local
preservation](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/local-preservation.html),
[global
preservation](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/global-preservation.html),
or [label
retrieval](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/label-retrieval.html).

For a worked example, pick the question closest to yours.

- Can you trust the digit next to yours in a UMAP plot? [Compare PCA,
  UMAP and t-SNE on
  MNIST](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/mnist-pca-umap.html).
- What happens to the scores when two digits set the scale of a map?
  [Compare two LTSA
  fits](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/ltsa-map-spread.html).
- Should a map preserve distances across a fold or along the sheet?
  [Unroll a Swiss
  roll](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/reference-geometry.html).
- How can two clouds merge while their short distances still look
  perfect? [Compare the
  bands](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/distance-band-fidelity.html).

## Acknowledgments

[ZADU](https://github.com/hj-n/zadu), the Python library by Hyeon Jeon
and colleagues, pointed me to several measures, including the [Gap
Index](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28324) of Ros, Arleo and Paulovich.
For Steadiness and Cohesiveness, Quadra follows ZADU 0.5.4 in how it
weights shared neighbors and how it combines losses in the pointwise
maps.

- [drnb](https://github.com/jlmelville/drnb) inspired three comparisons
  in Quadra. I compare the distance ranks of sampled pairs, estimate
  stress from sampled pairs, and compare counts of reciprocal neighbors
  between spaces.
- The distance-band profile comes from [Yoshio Takaeda’s
  benchmark](https://github.com/toorpia/dr-fidelity-benchmark). It asks
  how well distances are preserved among pairs that fall within a given
  radius in the input.
- For the Class Angular Distortion Index, Quadra follows [Gunaratne,
  Kobourov and Miller’s code](https://github.com/KaviruGunaratne/cadi).
  The cosine of an angle can change by at most two, so dividing the mean
  squared change by four puts the score on a scale from zero to one.
- The idea of comparing distance distributions with Earth Mover’s
  Distance comes from [Heiser and Lau’s work on single-cell
  data](https://github.com/KenLauLab/DR-structure-preservation). Quadra
  estimates those distributions by sampling pairs of observations.

# Package index

## Local neighborhood preservation

Compare neighbors or rank agreement between the input and embedding.

- [`nbr_pres()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/nbr_pres.md)
  : Neighborhood Preservation Between Distance Matrices
- [`nbr_pres_knn()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/nbr_pres_knn.md)
  : Neighborhood Preservation Between Nearest Neighbor Matrices
- [`nn_preservation()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/nn_preservation.md)
  : Nearest Neighbor Preservation
- [`trustworthiness()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/trustworthiness.md)
  [`continuity()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/trustworthiness.md)
  : Trustworthiness and Continuity Between Distance Matrices
- [`pointwise_rank_preservation()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/pointwise_rank_preservation.md)
  : Pointwise Trustworthiness and Continuity
- [`exact_rank_profiles()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/exact_rank_profiles.md)
  : Exact Rank Profiles from Euclidean Coordinates
- [`rnx_curve()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/rnx_curve.md)
  : RNX Curve
- [`rnx_auc()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/rnx_auc.md)
  : Area Under the RNX Curve
- [`pointwise_rnx()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/pointwise_rnx.md)
  : Pointwise RNX Agreement Across Neighborhood Sizes

## Local and regional geometry

Compare neighborhood shape, regional area, radii, and shared or
reciprocal neighbors.

- [`local_procrustes()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/local_procrustes.md)
  : Local Procrustes Error
- [`gap_index()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/gap_index.md)
  : Gap Index for Two-Dimensional Embeddings
- [`local_radius_correlation()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/local_radius_correlation.md)
  : Local Radius Correlation
- [`mutual_neighbor_correlation()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/mutual_neighbor_correlation.md)
  : Mutual Neighbor Correlation
- [`neighbor_dissimilarity()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/neighbor_dissimilarity.md)
  : Neighbor Dissimilarity Between Two Graphs

## Global distance preservation

Compare sampled distances and distance orderings.

- [`random_triplet_accuracy()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/random_triplet_accuracy.md)
  : Random Triplet Accuracy
- [`random_pair_distance_correlation()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/random_pair_distance_correlation.md)
  : Random Pair Distance Correlation
- [`random_pair_distance_emd()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/random_pair_distance_emd.md)
  : Earth Mover's Distance Between Random-Pair Distances
- [`random_pair_distance_stress()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/random_pair_distance_stress.md)
  : Random Pair Distance Stress
- [`random_pair_distance_band_profile()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/random_pair_distance_band_profile.md)
  : Distance-Band Fidelity for Random Pairs

## Label retrieval and class geometry

Measure label retrieval, centroid consistency, and angular distortion.

- [`roc_auc()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/roc_auc.md)
  : Average ROC AUC for Label Retrieval
- [`pr_auc()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/pr_auc.md)
  : Average Precision-Recall AUC for Label Retrieval
- [`class_pair_auc()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/class_pair_auc.md)
  : Retrieval AUC Within Each Pair of Classes
- [`label_trustworthiness_continuity()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/label_trustworthiness_continuity.md)
  : Label Trustworthiness and Continuity
- [`class_angular_distortion_index()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/class_angular_distortion_index.md)
  : Class Angular Distortion Index

## Group preservation

- [`steadiness_cohesiveness()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/steadiness_cohesiveness.md)
  : Steadiness and Cohesiveness of Groups

## Sampling helpers

Sample observation pairs or anchored triplets.

- [`sample_pairs()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/sample_pairs.md)
  : Sample Observation Pairs
- [`sample_triplets()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/sample_triplets.md)
  : Sample Anchored Triplets
- [`sample_class_triplets()`](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/reference/sample_class_triplets.md)
  : Sample Triplets for Class Angular Distortion

# Articles

### Guides

- [Metric
  overview](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/metrics-overview.md):

  Choose a metric from the relationship your embedding should preserve.

- [Local
  preservation](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/local-preservation.md):

  Choose and interpret metrics for neighbor identity, rank, local scale,
  graph structure, and multiple neighborhood sizes.

- [Global
  preservation](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/global-preservation.md):

  Choose and interpret sampled metrics for global distance order,
  association, distributions, and matched magnitudes.

- [Label
  retrieval](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/label-retrieval.md):

  Choose ROC or precision-recall AUC and inspect overall, per-label, and
  per-query retrieval scores.

### Workflows

- [Evaluating PCA, UMAP and t-SNE on
  MNIST](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/mnist-pca-umap.md):

  Compare neighborhood, distance, and label preservation on the same
  digits.

- [When two digits set the scale of an LTSA
  map](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/ltsa-map-spread.md):

  Compare neighbor overlap and fitted-scale stress on MNIST, then change
  the reference on a Swiss roll.

- [Which distances should a Swiss roll
  preserve?](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/reference-geometry.md):

  Evaluate PCA and LTSA against rolled and intrinsic geometry.

- [Distance fidelity across
  scales](https://jlmelville.github.io/quadra/articles/distance-band-fidelity.md):

  Compare distance order and magnitude from nearby input pairs to the
  whole dataset.
